name: Zabdi
overview: Zabdi was a male member of the tribe of Judah known primarily as the father of Carmi and Achan. His identity is noted in the context of Achan's transgression involving the taking of forbidden items from Jericho, highlighting his role within a significant biblical incident. No additional personal notes are recorded.
namesAndTitles: The name Zabdi means 'YHWH bestows,' reflecting a theologically meaningful Hebrew name. Another related name, Zimri, means 'wild goats, sheep; possibly awe of YHWH,' indicating a connection to the tribe of Judah and reverence toward God. Both names are proper names not specifically given by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Zabdi explicitly as the father of Zerah and infers him as the father of Carmi. Through Carmi, Zabdi is also the father of Achan, whose actions are significant in the biblical narrative. These relationships establish Zabdi's family line within Judah.
scriptureSignificance: Zabdi's significance in Scripture arises chiefly from his connection to Achan, whose violation of God's command regarding the spoils of Jericho brought judgment upon Israel. As the patriarch of this family line, Zabdi is indirectly linked to this pivotal event, which underscores the seriousness of obedience to God's instructions during Israel's conquest of Canaan.
